arxiv-1604-03635.title: Online Multi-Target Tracking Using Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-1604-03635.creator: Anton Milan 1, S. Hamid Rezatofighi 1, Anthony Dick 1, Ian Reid 1, Konrad Schindler 2, 2 schindler@geod.baug.ethz.ch
arxiv-1604-03635.description: Abstract We present a novel approach to online multi-target tracking based on recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Tracking multiple objects in real-world scenes involves many challenges, including a) an a-priori unknown and time-varying number of targets, b) a continuous state estimation of all present targets, and c) a discrete combinatorial problem of data association.

arxiv-2106-05400.title: Fine-Grained System Identification of Nonlinear Neural Circuits Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2021; Virtual Event, Singapore Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’21
arxiv-2106-05400.creator: Dawna Bagherian, James Gornet, Jeremy Bernstein, Yu-Li Ni, Yisong Yue, Markus Meister
arxiv-2106-05400.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dawna Bagherian, James Gornet, Jeremy Bernstein, Yu-Li Ni, Yisong Yue, Markus Meister. We study the problem of sparse nonlinear model recovery of high dimensional compositional functions. Our study is motivated by emerging opportunities in neuroscience to recover fine-grained models of biological neural circuits using collected measurement data. Guided by available domain knowledge in neuroscience, we explore conditions under which one can recover the underlying biological circuit that generated the training data. Our results suggest insights of both theoretical and practical interests.

arxiv-2210-07448.creator: Stefan Larson 1 , 3 {}^{~~1,3} &Gordon Lim 2 &Yutong Ai 2 &David Kuang 2 &Kevin Leach 3 and 1 DryvIQ 2 University of Michigan 3 Vanderbilt University Ann Arbor, MI, USA Ann Arbor, MI, USA Nashville, TN, USA
arxiv-2210-07448.description: Abstract The ability of a document classifier to handle inputs that are drawn from a distribution different from the training distribution is crucial for robust deployment and generalizability. The RVL-CDIP corpus [ 18 ] is the de facto standard benchmark for document classification, yet to our knowledge all studies that use this corpus do not include evaluation on out-of-distribution documents.

arxiv-2301-06484.title: Algebraic Wasserstein distances and stable homological invariants of data
arxiv-2301-06484.creator: Jens Agerberg, Andrea Guidolin, Isaac Ren, Martina Scolamiero
arxiv-2301-06484.description: Abstract Distances have a ubiquitous role in persistent homology, from the direct comparison of homological representations of data to the definition and optimization of invariants. In this article we introduce a family of parametrized pseudometrics between persistence modules based on the algebraic Wasserstein distance defined by Skraba and Turner, and phrase them in the formalism of noise systems.

arxiv-2306-17737.description: Abstract In order to solve tasks like uncertainty quantification or hypothesis tests in Bayesian imaging inverse problems, we often have to draw samples from the arising posterior distribution. For the usually log-concave but high-dimensional posteriors, Markov chain Monte Carlo methods based on time discretizations of Langevin diffusion are a popular tool.

arxiv-2505-06033.creator: Vojtěch David, Dmitriy N. Zhuk
arxiv-2505-06033.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vojtěch David, Dmitriy N. Zhuk. We introduce a new approach to the description of multi-sorted clones (sets of k k -tuples of operations of the same arity, closed under coordinatewise composition and containing all projection tuples) on a two-element domain. Leveraging the well-known Galois connection between operations and relations, we define a small class of canonical relations sufficient to describe all Boolean multi-sorted clones up to non-surjective operations.

arxiv-2510-16917.description: Abstract Knowledge editing offers an efficient way to update model knowledge without full retraining, but prior work has concentrated almost exclusively on textual or visual modalities.
